title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 21 November 2026
headline: Supreme Court Permits One-Time Karthigai Deepam Lighting at Tiruparankundram Amid Intense Political Friction and Opposition Backlash

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is currently dominated by fierce controversy surrounding the Supreme Court's interim order permitting a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the disputed 'Deepathoon' atop Madurai's Tiruparankundram hill on November 24, 2026. While opposition figures and communal watchdogs like VCK chief Thol. Thirumavalavan have sharply condemned the verdict as an invitation to social discord, PMK leaders such as Sowmiya Anbumani have hailed it as a historic realization of public sentiment. Meanwhile, inter-party tensions have escalated on multiple fronts, with DMK President M.K. Stalin slamming Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's administration over alleged plans to relocate the state Secretariat to Pattinapakkam at the expense of traditional fishing communities.

Governance and economic policy have also triggered friction, as the opposition scrutinizes the TVK government over alleged data leaks and staff attrition at investment promotion agency Guidance Tamil Nadu. Despite these controversies, Industries Minister S. Keerthana reported that the administration has successfully signed 112 Memorandums of Understanding worth Rs 1,14,811.91 crore, projecting 1,32,771 new jobs during its first six months in office. Simultaneously, the Madras High Court has been proactive, issuing strict directives ranging from state-wide bans on wandering livestock on public roads to mandating the installation of AI-powered tracking systems to prevent elephant fatalities along railway corridors, setting a benchmark for neighboring Kerala.

The apex bench stayed the earlier Madras High Court order that had barred the ritual while explicitly forbidding public entry to the hilltop site to maintain public order. sections.government_and_administration: - **Anbumani Urges Immediate Scrapping of Rs 450 Crore Vellalore Waste-to-Energy Project:** PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss strongly demanded that the Tamil Nadu government permanently scrap the proposed Rs 450 crore waste-to-energy plant in Vellalore, Coimbatore, citing severe environmental and public health hazards. Ramadoss criticized the TVK administration for issuing commercial tenders despite sustained, vocal opposition from local resident welfare associations and independent environmental monitoring groups. He asserted that burning municipal solid waste through the current plant design would transform Coimbatore into a toxic pollution hotspot, triggering respiratory illnesses across densely populated municipal wards. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/anbumani-seeks-scrapping-of-rs-450-crore-waste-to-energy-plant-in-coimbatore))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **Dushyant Dave Criticizes TVK Government for Discontinuing Justice Kurian Joseph Committee:** Senior Supreme Court advocate Dushyant Dave publicly rebuked the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government for unilaterally winding up the Justice Kurian Joseph committee on Union-State relations, arguing that the decision exposes a fundamental lack of political foresight. Speaking on the sidelines of ongoing legal discussions, Dave revealed that former Supreme Court judge Justice Kurian Joseph himself expressed profound surprise over the state's abrupt decision to scrap the panel amid critical threats of parliamentary constituency delimitation. Opposition parties have seized upon Dave's remarks to lambetate the ruling administration for compromising state autonomy and weakening institutional frameworks designed to safeguard federal rights. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/scrapping-kurian-panel-a-mistake-amid-delimitation-threat-senior-advocate-dushyant-dave))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Directs Kerala to Implement Tamil Nadu's AI Camera Model for Elephant Conservation:** In a significant environmental ruling, the Madras High Court ordered the Kerala government to replicate Tamil Nadu's successful technological framework by installing artificial intelligence-enabled cameras along forest railway tracks to prevent accidental jumbo deaths. The bench emphasized that inter-state coordination and proactive technological intervention are mandatory to protect endangered wildlife traversing vulnerable Western Ghat corridors. Additionally, the High Court issued comprehensive state-wide administrative directions prohibiting owners from allowing stray livestock to wander on public roadways, mandating strict penalties for municipal negligence. ([The Hindu](https://news.google.?oc=5))
sections.district_developments: - **Political Rivals and Cinema Icons Share Stage at High-Profile Wedding Reception:** Prominent political adversaries and leading figures from the Tamil cinema industry converged in Chennai on November 21, 2026, for the high-profile wedding reception of music composer Anirudh and Kavya. Chief Minister and TVK president C. Joseph Vijay, DMK president M.K. Stalin, and AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami shared the spotlight, creating a rare moment of bipartisan bonhomie away from the blazing electoral arena. While the gathering remained strictly social, political observers closely tracked the interactions between the ruling party leadership and veteran opposition chiefs amidst tightening political competition across urban districts. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/political-rivals-cinema-veterans-share-spotlight-at-anirudh-kavya-wedding-reception/article71729098.ece))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, all political and administrative eyes will be locked on Madurai as district authorities enforce the Supreme Court's stringent security protocols for the one-time Karthigai Deepam lighting at the Tiruparankundram 'Deepathoon' scheduled for November 24. Observers will closely monitor police compliance with the absolute ban on public entry to the hilltop, alongside potential statements from opposition parties regarding the state's handling of the event. Simultaneously, legal experts will track any supplementary petitions filed in the Madras High Court concerning municipal waste projects and coastal environmental clearances.
